To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presence of a phage prophage confers intrinsic resistance to PhEf11 lysin.
lysogeny of E. facealis with phage PhEf 11 is the primary mechanism by which the bacterium acquires resistance to the PhEf11 endolysin.
intrinsic resistance of Enterococcal strains to PhEf1 phage endolysis is associated with the lysogenic conversion of the strains.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a novel mechanism of resistance to a phage encoded murein lytic enzyme.
the use of bacteriophages as a novel approach for controlling multidrug resistant enterococci.
the development of a phage lysin based antimicrobial therapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the lysin is effective against the vast majority of clinical strains of E. faecealis, but that a small number of strains (less than 5%) may be lysin resistant due to prophage mediated resistance.
the lysin resistance of the PhEf11 prophages is a direct result of the prophage being integrated into the chromosome.
lysin resistance is associated with the prophage.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intrinsic resistance of E. faealis strains to ORF28 phage endolynis is associated with the prophage.
the PhEf11 lysin is a highly potent antimicrobial agent, but that the presence of prophage PhEf11 in E. faecialis strains may confer intrinsic resistance.
the PhEf11 lysin is a promising antimicrobial agent for use against E. faecali, however, the prophage is an obstacle to the widespread use of the lysin as a therapeutic or prophylactic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a prophage is a major determinant for the sensitivity of E. faecealis strains to the PhEf11 ORFs28 endolysin.
the presence of PhEff1 prophage is a reliable predictor of PhEf11 lysin insensitivity.
lysin resistance is not an intrinsic characteristic of E. faecealis, but rather, is acquired through the presence of prophage.
